subject: mathematics
question_text: The sum of two numbers a and b is 6 times their geometric mean. Show that the numbers are in the ratio (3 + 2√2) : (3 − 2√2).

mark_split.label: Write the condition as a ratio and apply componendo and dividendo
Apply the rule again and square

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name the rule you apply and say what perfect squares appear.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the condition as a ratio and apply componendo and dividendo
steps.margin_note: First mark. The examiner looks for the ratio written as (a + b)/(2√(ab)) = 3/1 and for the rule named.
steps.memory_tip: Componendo and dividendo turns p/q = r/s into (p + q)/(p − q) = (r + s)/(r − s).

recall.must_convey: That the condition is written as (a + b)/(2√(ab)) = 3/1 and componendo and dividendo gives (√a + √b)/(√a − √b) = √2.
accept: write a plus b over two root a b equals three by one
a plus b plus two root a b is root a plus root b whole squared
componendo dividendo apply cheste perfect square vasthundi
divide by two root a b first then use the rule

steps.why: Writing the condition as the ratio 3 : 1 sets up componendo and dividendo, and a + b ± 2√(ab) are exactly the perfect squares (√a ± √b)².
common_mistakes: Halving only one side and writing (a + b)/√(ab) = 3.
Not seeing that a + b + 2√(ab) is (√a + √b)².

steps.label: Apply the rule again and square

recall.must_convey: That a second use of componendo and dividendo gives √a/√b = (√2 + 1)/(√2 − 1), and squaring gives the required ratio.
accept: use componendo and dividendo a second time
root a by root b is root two plus one over root two minus one
square both sides to get three plus two root two
malli componendo dividendo apply chesi square cheyyali
the squares give three plus two root two and three minus two root two

steps.why: The second use of the rule isolates √a and √b, and squaring removes the roots. Expanding (√2 ± 1)² is what produces the required form.
common_mistakes: Writing (√2 + 1)² = 2 + 1 = 3 and dropping the cross term 2√2.
Stopping at √a/√b and not squaring to reach a : b.
